justification: Standard: adds 7 data files that the housing-reform area check reads to measure real walking distance. Not Minor: it changes what the check answers (yes/no/borderline instead of can't tell) for 7 pilot councils. Not Critical: no schema, no database write, no new code path in the decision logic; the files are read by the existing, already-tested reader and an unreadable file still gives 'can't tell'.

pre_impl.existing_data: Walking files existed for 5 areas only (cb-bankstown, georges-river, inner-west x3, kuringgai, woollahra), covering 3 of the 10 pilot councils. The other 7 returned can't-tell when a lot was inside 800 m straight line. Station entrances already in data/law/lmr_station_entrances.json; town centres from the Town Centres layer.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I first said the walk was not measured at all; it is measured, and walk_m is null only when the straight line already exceeds 800 m (a walk cannot be shorter). The real gap was coverage, not method.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Same builder (build_walk_surfaces.py) and packer (pack_walk_surfaces.py) as the existing five areas, one area per council, no code change to the reader or the rules. Only change to scripts: an optional --boxes argument and an LMR_CAP env var on the test script so it can draw lots from other areas.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Footpaths are OpenStreetMap data and the judge router is also OpenStreetMap-based, so both can share a missing path. The test shows agreement between two methods, not ground truth.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A wrong 'yes' would tell a user a lot is in the housing area when it is not. The rules show a range and 'borderline' near the limit, and say 'can't tell' when no footpath is within 40 m.

falsifiable_check.command: LMR_SURF_DIR=../lmr_walk python scripts/lmr_area/area_check_test.py --n 100 --seed 20261117 --boxes=<council bboxes>  then scripts/lmr_area/area_check_score.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The new files are absent: lots in the 7 councils fall back to 'walking_measure_unavailable' (can't tell) instead of a measured walk, so the can't-tell share rises well above 5%.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before these files, the walking reader had no surface for these councils; lots inside 800 m straight line returned cant_tell(walking_measure_unavailable). With the files: 4 of 182 real can't-tell (2.2%), 122 of 122 yes/no answers agree with the independent router (0 opposite), range holds 88 of 97 (91%). Run on 2 fresh 100-lot sets plus 3 top-ups, seeds 20261117, 20261118, 20261121-23, 20261131-32.

functions.name: load_surface
functions.input: path to a packed .npz walking file
functions.output: Surface with distances, anchors, bbox; rejects files with too few nodes
functions.if_none: unreadable or invalid file gives can't-tell, never a guessed distance

functions.name: test_exactly_the_expected_walking_files_exist
functions.input: the folder data/lmr_walk searched for all .npz walking files
functions.output: pins the exact file list so an unexpected file or a missing file fails
functions.if_none: an empty folder fails the comparison, so a missing file cannot pass silently

values: N/A - no value is read from a database or API at runtime by this change; the new files hold precomputed footpath distances.
queries: N/A - no database query. Lots were drawn from the NSW Property layer by the test script only.

break_it.scenario: A wrong 'yes' outside the 7 new councils: 19 Ryde Road, Pymble (Ku-ring-gai) says yes at 548 m, router says 1,055 m.
break_it.what_happens: That lot would show in the housing area when the router says it is not.
break_it.how: Not caused by these files (Ku-ring-gai file is unchanged). Cause not yet diagnosed; logged as an open item, not hidden.
break_it.repro: python scripts/lmr_area/area_check_test.py --boxes=-33.80,151.12,-33.74,151.16 and look at 19 RYDE ROAD PYMBLE

break_it.scenario: A lot has no footpath within 40 m of the surface.
break_it.what_happens: Answer is can't-tell with reason walking_measure_unavailable, never a made-up distance.
break_it.repro: 4 such lots in the 182 tested, all reported as can't-tell

break_it.scenario: A new .npz is over the repo file limit or has too few nodes.
break_it.what_happens: Pre-commit large-file gate blocks the commit, or the reader refuses the file.
break_it.how: test_walking_files_exist_fit_the_repo_limit_and_load checks size under 2 MB and MIN_NODES; largest file is 554,300 bytes

break_it.scenario: A walking file is added but not copied into the deployed image.
break_it.what_happens: Deployed lots get a reason and no area.
break_it.how: Dockerfile.python already copies the whole data/lmr_walk/ folder; test_the_python_image_copies_every_file_the_area_check_reads covers it

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after deploy, run the area check on one lot per new council against the live API and confirm a measured walk, not can't-tell.
